key_insight: Small sampled PDE residuals can mask O(1) value errors: PINNs may learn almost-everywhere Hamilton–Jacobi solutions rather than the correct viscosity solution.
engineering_relevance: For pursuit–evasion value estimation, network parameterization and independent structural checks can be essential to avoid accepting incorrect solutions.
method: Compare four neural parameterizations on fixed-horizon pursuit–evasion games with closed-form values on S¹, T², and T⁴.
Test periodic Fourier features, loss-enforced periodicity, distance-informed inputs, and minimum-over-image-chart models.
Use a mesh-free finite-difference semiconcavity diagnostic requiring only forward network evaluations.
evidence_signal: Across 120 runs, Fourier-feature networks learned folded incorrect solutions in all 30 trials; wrapped-displacement-plus-distance inputs recovered the viscosity solution in 30/30, versus 27/30 for minimum-over-chart models.
watch_item: Results concern a specific pursuit–evasion problem; the diagnostic relies on semiconcavity for the convex Hamiltonian studied, so broader applicability needs validation.
paper_title: Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
